text:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV2 - streaming-api-prod p99 latency breach (streaming stalls / chunking delays). Alerting on > 2s p99 for streaming endpoints. Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream. Started: 1746001123. Auto-tags: #streaming #latency #sse

ash_sre_oncall: I'm on it. Initial question: is this affecting all regions or just us-east-1?

lee_runtime_eng: I'm seeing elevated tail latency from the proxy layer in logs, looks like several connections are paused then burst. Running quick curl against SSE endpoint now.

lee_runtime_eng: curl test shows long gaps between chunks:
```
$ curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://streaming-api.prod/v1/stream?model=redwood-7b
data: {"id":"tok","text":"hello"}

(4s silence)

data: {"id":"tok","text":" world"}
```

ana_prod_support: Customer John from Acme reported slow streaming in last 10 minutes, says UI shows spinner for ~6s before any tokens appear.

marta_infra: Check envoy upstream_timeout and downstream_socket_timeout - we rolled a change to default chunk flush behavior earlier this week. I'm looking at the config now.

ash_sre_oncall: Quick triage checklist:
- confirm p95/p99 deltas (Grafana)
- check proxy (envoy) and sidecar logs for backpressure
- verify pod-level CPU/RAM and epoll wait stats
- try temporary mitigation (increase proxy chunk flush frequency / route to fallback service)

lee_runtime_eng: Grafana: p95 up from 120ms -> 380ms; p99 from 680ms -> 2.4s. Error rate unchanged. Streaming-specific endpoints have the worst tail.

lee_runtime_eng: Envoy logs: lots of "upstream response timeout" entries but responses then arrive later rather than failing. Suggests buffering on proxy side. Sample:
```
[2026-03-14T14:05:12Z] envoy upstream response timeout: stream_id=0x7f, route=/v1/stream
[2026-03-14T14:05:16Z] envoy flush: wrote 1 chunk to downstream, bytes=256
```

ash_sre_oncall: That matches client reports (long spinner then chunk). Could be chunk coalescing due to Nagle/linger or our flush threshold.

lee_runtime_eng: Quick mitigation proposal: flip the feature flag that enabled chunk_coalesce=auto, forcing immediate flush on token ready. If we can toggle that via runtime config, do it. Also bump proxy downstream_socket_timeout to 30s from 15s to avoid premature upstream timeouts while we observe.

marta_infra: I can flip the runtime flag for streaming-prod in 1 minute. Will also patch envoy config on canary pods first.

ana_prod_support: @john_cust_sre can you ask the Acme contact to capture HAR or repro steps? They mentioned Chrome only. Might be client-side buffering too.

john_cust_sre: I'll ping them; they're on a call. They say it reproduces in Chrome and Safari, so likely server side.

ash_sre_oncall: Do we risk any regressions by toggling flush? What about CPU impact?

lee_runtime_eng: Immediate flush will increase syscall frequency and slightly raise CPU usage for streamer pods, but should be safe for short mitigation. We'll monitor CPU% and p50/p95. If CPU rises >15% we rollback.

marta_infra: Runtime flag toggled on canary (streamer-3). Observing canary logs now.

lee_runtime_eng: Canary shows chunk spacing reduced to ~60ms. p99 on canary route dropped to 420ms. 

ash_sre_oncall: Rollout to 50% (blue/green) for streaming-prod. Keep alerting thresholds lowered to catch regressions.

marta_infra: Rolled to 50%. Envoy timeout bumped to 30s canary applied.

lee_runtime_eng: After 50% rollout, global p99 is down to 1.1s and counting down. UI reports from customers show tokens now arriving steadily instead of big gaps.

ana_prod_support: Acme confirms much better behavior after our changes. They still see occasional ~1s gaps but acceptable for now.

ash_sre_oncall: Good. Next steps: keep mitigations in place for 2 hours while we root cause. Logging pointers: enable detailed tcp_keepalive and flush-debug for streamer pods. Capture netstat/epoll stats.

lee_runtime_eng: Probable root causes to investigate:
- recent chunk_coalesce change that batched small writes to reduce syscalls
- envoys with differing HTTP/1.1 chunk flush semantics (we saw a config change last Wed)
- client-side TCP push buffering (socket options) interacting with Nagle/PSH timing

marta_infra: Will audit config change PRs affecting envoy and runtime-flags between 3/8 - 3/12.

ash_sre_oncall: Handoff to night oncall @ash_next at 1746002000. I'll annotate runbook and mitigation steps in the incident doc. Postmortem owner: lee_runtime_eng.

lee_runtime_eng: Noted. I'll schedule a deeper trace extraction and pair with infra to reproduce locally with high fanout.

ash_sre_oncall: Summary for customer comms: cause under investigation, immediate mitigation applied (forced flush + proxy timeout bump), visible improvement, ongoing RCA, will follow up with timeline and root cause. Ana can draft a short update to Acme.

ana_prod_support: Drafting now, ETA 10m.

marta_infra: Adding a follow-up PR to make flush defaults conservative and opt-in for coalescing.

ash_sre_oncall: Closing incident thread for active paging; keeping channel open for updates. If p99 creeps back above 2s, page SRE again. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated at 1746001790. Severity reduced to SEV3.

ash_sre_oncall: Leaving notes:
- Mitigation: runtime flag forced_flush=true, envoy downstream_socket_timeout=30s, 50% rollout then full after positive metrics
- Observed impact window: 1746001123 - 1746001790
- Postmortem: scheduled for 1746070000 (next day) with lee as owner

lee_runtime_eng: I'll attach traces and a reproducer repo before the postmortem.

john_cust_sre: Acme acknowledges fix and appreciates quick response.

ash_sre_oncall: Thanks team. If anyone sees residual issues, reply here and we'll re-open paging.
